name: M5Stack Unit Dual Button
description: Grove unit from M5Stack with two 12 mm push buttons (blue and red caps). Each button shorts its signal line to GND; at rest the line sits on a 10 kOhm / 20 kOhm divider from the 5 V Grove supply (with 100 nF filtering), so it reads about 3.3 V when released and 0 V when pressed (active low). No chip, no pull-up needed on the GPIO. Sold as: M5Stack Unit Dual Button (SKU U025), 48 x 24 mm unit with HY2.0-4P Grove socket BLUE (white), RED (yellow), 5V, GND.
eli5: Two buttons, one blue and one red, on a Grove cable: each one pulls its own wire to 0 V while you press it.

pins.name: BLUE
pins.description: Blue button (Grove pin 1, white wire, schematic net A): about 3.3 V (10k/20k divider from 5 V) while released, 0 V while pressed. Safe for 3.3 V GPIOs when the unit runs from 5 V.

pins.name: RED
pins.description: Red button (Grove pin 2, yellow wire, schematic net B): about 3.3 V while released, 0 V while pressed.

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: Supply (Grove pin 3, red wire): 5 V. It feeds the 10k/20k dividers that set the released level, so use 5 V, not 3.3 V.

buildNotes: Grove connector order (M5Stack schematic J1): pin 1 A = BLUE button (white wire), pin 2 B = RED button (yellow wire), pin 3 VCC (red wire), pin 4 GND (black wire). The unit has a HY2.0-4P Grove socket: use a Grove-to-female-jumper cable for a breadboard.

Power it from 5 V (ESP32 5V/VIN, Pico VBUS). The released level is 5 V x 20k/30k = 3.33 V, so the lines connect straight to 3.3 V GPIOs. From 3.3 V the released level would be only ~2.2 V, too low for a reliable logic 1.
Both buttons are active LOW: 1 while released, 0 while pressed. No GPIO pull-up is needed (the divider sets the level); input-only pins such as ESP32 GPIO34-39 work.
On an M5Stack Core plug it into Port B: blue = GPIO36 (white), red = GPIO26 (yellow).
Contacts bounce for a few ms; the 100 nF + divider filter smooths it a little, and the driver debounces for 20 ms.

example.code:
from m5_dual_button import M5DualButton
import time

buttons = M5DualButton({BLUE}, {RED})
while True:
    print('BLUE=%d RED=%d' % buttons.read())
    time.sleep(0.3)

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (4 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
